hook: $24.77 pillows do more work than your headboard

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen: a flat two-pillow bed on the left, a boutique hotel bed with a graduated pillow stack on the right
scenes.voiceover: Strip a hotel bed photo down to what's actually doing the work, and it's not the headboard.

scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of a pillow seam, fingers pointing to the gusseted side panel stitched into the edge
scenes.voiceover: That extra strip of fabric in the seam is called a gusset, and it's the reason hotel pillows hold loft instead of going flat.

scenes.visual_prompt: Amazon-listing-style graphic overlay showing 4.5 stars, 79,136 ratings, and $24.77 price on a queen pillow pair
scenes.voiceover: This queen gusseted pillow set is $24.77 for two, and it's one of the highest-reviewed pillow listings on Amazon.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands stacking four pillows in graduated height on a made bed, standard pillows in back and a folded sham in front
scenes.voiceover: Buy two sets, stack standard pillows in back and a folded sham in front — that's the layering hotels actually use.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of the finished bed with full pillow stack in front of the panel wall
scenes.voiceover: Two sets runs just under fifty dollars, still inside the budget of the panel wall itself.

scenes.visual_prompt: Before and after split screen of the same bed frame with only the pillows changed
scenes.voiceover: The headboard didn't change. The pillows did.

caption: I went looking for the one detail that makes a hotel bed photo work, and it's not the headboard — it's the gusset in the pillow seam. Full comparison on the blog, link in bio.
